memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Obesity assessment and initiation of therapy.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: The patient presents for weight management, reporting gradual weight gain over the past year and concerns about health risks.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 92 kg, height 160 cm, BMI 35.9 (obese per Asian cut‑offs). Abdomen soft, no tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 35.9. No hypertension or dyslipidaemia noted clinically.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start orlistat 120 mg with each main meal. Advise reduced‑calorie diet, increase physical activity to 150 min/week. Return if severe abdominal pain, oily stools with bleeding, fever >39°C, or sudden shortness of breath.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Orlistat 120 mg PO TID with breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Continue for 3 months, then review.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.8 mmol/L (ref <5.2), LDL 2.9 mmol/L (<2.6), HDL 1.2 mmol/L (>1.0), triglycerides 1.6 mmol/L (<1.7). Fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5) slightly elevated. HbA1c 5.8% (4.0‑5.6) mildly raised. Liver function: ALT 28 U/L (<40), AST 24 U/L (<38), ALP 78 U/L (40‑129), GGT 32 U/L (<51).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up on obesity therapy after 3 months.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports modest weight loss, improved energy, no GI side‑effects.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/84 mmHg, weight 90 kg, BMI 35.2 (obese). Abdomen benign.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 35.2, modest response to orlistat. Lipids and glucose improved but still above target.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue orlistat 120 mg TID. Reinforce diet (500 kcal deficit) and brisk walking 30 min daily. Return if persistent oily stools, abdominal cramping, vomiting, fever >39°C, or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Orlistat 120 mg PO TID with meals. Continue for another 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.5 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.6 mmol/L (≤2.6), HDL 1.3 mmol/L (>1.0), triglycerides 1.4 mmol/L (<1.7). Fasting glucose 5.4 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5). HbA1c 5.6% (4.0‑5.6) at upper limit. LFT: ALT 22, AST 20, ALP 75, GGT 30 (all within normal).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Six‑month obesity review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes weight plateau, occasional dietary lapses.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 89 kg, BMI 34.8 (obese). No abdominal tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 34.8, stable on orlistat. Metabolic parameters within normal range except borderline HbA1c.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue orlistat 120 mg TID. Counsel on mindful eating, increase aerobic activity to 180 min/week. Return if severe diarrhoea, rectal bleeding, unexplained weight loss, fever >39°C, or palpitations.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.6 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.7 mmol/L (≤2.6) slightly high, HDL 1.2 mmol/L (>1.0), triglycerides 1.5 mmol/L (<1.7). Fasting glucose 5.5 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5). HbA1c 5.7% (4.0‑5.6) mildly elevated. LFT: ALT 24, AST 22, ALP 80, GGT 34 (normal).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Weight management check‑in after holiday period.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports slight weight regain, festive eating.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/82 mmHg, weight 90 kg, BMI 35.2 (obese). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 35.2, modest weight fluctuation. Labs remain acceptable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Reinforce orlistat adherence, set SMART goals for diet (≤1500 kcal/day) and activity. Return if worsening GI symptoms, fever >39°C, dyspnoea on exertion, or chest discomfort.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Orlistat 120 mg PO TID with main meals. Continue for 3 months, then reassess.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Obesity follow‑up; medication tolerance reviewed.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports increased oily stools and abdominal discomfort after meals.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/84 mmHg, weight 91 kg, BMI 35.5 (obese). Mild lower abdominal tenderness, no masses.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 35.5, possible orlistat intolerance contributing to GI symptoms.
ARRANGEMENTS: Discuss stopping orlistat due to side‑effects. Advise low‑fat diet (<30% fat) to reduce symptoms, increase fibre, maintain activity. Return if severe diarrhoea, dehydration, fever >39°C, or rectal bleeding.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Orlistat discontinued per patient request. No further supply.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been having oily, foul‑smelling stools and mild cramps since starting orlistat. I think I should stop the medication and try diet alone.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Off‑orlistat obesity review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports stopped orlistat 2 months ago, weight stable, GI symptoms resolved.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80 mmHg, weight 92 kg, BMI 35.9 (obese). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 35.9, off pharmacotherapy. Lifestyle measures needed.
ARRANGEMENTS: Initiate structured diet plan (1200‑1500 kcal/day), prescribe aerobic exercise 150 min/week, consider behavioural counselling. Return if rapid weight gain, fever >39°C, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.0 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 3.0 mmol/L (≤2.6) slightly high, HDL 1.1 mmol/L (>1.0), triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (<1.7) borderline. Fasting glucose 5.8 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5) elevated. HbA1c 6.0% (4.0‑5.6) indicating pre‑diabetes. LFT: ALT 26, AST 23, ALP 82, GGT 35 (normal).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2026-09-20 at 10:00 with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03) for obesity follow‑up.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up after lifestyle intervention.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports adherence to reduced‑calorie diet and regular walking, feels more energetic.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 91.5 kg, BMI 35.4 (obese). Abdomen benign.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI 35.4, modest weight loss since July. Glucose and lipids still elevated but trending.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current diet and activity plan, re‑check labs in 3 months. Return if fever >39°C, chest pain, severe dyspnoea, or unexplained weight loss.
